newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs rise, fears of higher interest rates dwindle.
newsitem.headline: JGBs rise, fears of higher interest rates dwindle.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures were higher by midday on Monday, due to firmness of cash bonds, traders said.
"JGBs are up, retaining strong sentiment from LIFFE, but they were also boosted by firmness of cash bonds, such as the 193rd to 196th 10-year JGBs," a trader at a trust bank's securities unit said.

In the afternoon, market players would watch May Tokyo area department store sales due at 2.30 p.m. (0530 GMT) and, to a lesser extent, April revised industrial output data due at 1.30 p.m. (0430 GMT), traders said.
The September stood at 124.12 by midday, up from Friday's close of 123.85. Turnover was 15,883 contracts.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.365 percent, as of 0227 GMT, down from 2.390 percent on Friday.

Although scattered buying of cash bonds by investors such as city banks was detected in the morning, JGBs were heavy on top, due to talk of selling by regional investors, a trader for a city bank's securities unit said.
"Some investors seem to be buying bonds to meet investment plans for the July-September period. Life insurers, however, seem content to remain on the sidelines." the trader said.
JGBs are unlikely to rise substantially from current levels on Monday, as some players are eager to sell above 124.00, a trader for another city bank's securities unit said.
Traders also said the upside of JGBs is likely to be capped at around 124.50 on Monday as a key resistance point lies at 124.37.

The rise on LIFFE on Friday was due in part to buying of the September by a major brokerage house, a trust bank trader said. The September was also boosted on LIFFE by city banks' receiving of fixed interest rates and rises in euroyen futures on Friday, the trust bank trader said.
Euroyen futures rose on SIMEX based on speculation that the forthcoming Bank of Japan's key "tankan" corporate sentiment survey may show weak business sentiment, the trust bank trader said.
The market is gradually coming to a consensus that the results of the tankan will be weak, the first trader said.

"Industrial output has been weak, and although the (January-March) GDP data was strong, there is concern that the figures may have been pushed up by a consumption rush ahead of a rise in the consumption tax. Such views are leading to speculation that the tankan may turn out weak," he said.
Regarding the indicators due in the afternoon, some said May Tokyo area department store sales are likely to come in at around minus 3.5 percent year-on-year.
The revised industrial output data for April may induce some position adjustment, but it is not a big enough factor to alter the direction of the market, the first trader said.
If industrial output data for April is revised upwards, some selling may set in, at least temporarily, a trader for another trust bank's securities unit said.
The government's preliminary figures released in May showed Japan's industrial output fell 0.4 percent in April.
